Explore the gallery

Hardwood

Plan species, grade, direction, transitions, and site conditions.

Hardwood installation depends on substrate, moisture, acclimation, layout, fastening or adhesive strategy, and transitions to adjacent rooms.

Refinishing scope depends on the existing floor, wear layer, repairs, stain expectations, and occupied-home logistics.

LVP and laminate

Use resilient materials where their properties fit the room.

Product construction, substrate tolerances, expansion requirements, moisture exposure, transitions, and manufacturer instructions affect the result.

Material selection should account for the household rather than appearance alone.

Tile and refinishing

Resolve flatness, layout, edges, and adjacent finishes.

Tile flooring needs appropriate substrate preparation, movement accommodation, layout, grout, and transition details.

Refinishing requires dust-control planning, finish selection, cure time, and realistic expectations for existing damage.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Flooring Installation & Refinishing FAQs

Should hardwood and refinishing have separate pages?

Not at launch. They remain substantial sections of one Flooring page until project proof, leads, capacity, and search performance support a split.

What can delay flooring installation?

Subfloor repair, moisture, acclimation, material lead times, ongoing wet work, cabinetry or trim sequencing, and furniture logistics.

Can flooring run continuously through several rooms?

Often, but product requirements, substrate changes, movement, thresholds, room geometry, and installation direction need to be planned.
